description: Synthetic personal-notes corpus. 40 notes in 4 topic clusters (cooking, travel, programming, health) so that retrieval must separate similar notes. 5 queries per note: 3 'paraphrase' (little lexical overlap with the note) and 2 'keyword' (share rare terms). Each query has exactly one relevant note.

notes.title: Injera troubleshooting
notes.text:
My teff batter ferments for three days on the counter before it is ready. If the surface smells sharply sour and the bubbles stop, I skim off the water on top and start the absit step: cook one cup of the batter into a thin porridge, cool it, and stir it back in.
When the mitad is too hot the injera cracks at the edges, and when the batter is too thick the little eyes never form. Keep the lid on for about two minutes and don't flip it. Use a nonstick pan if the clay mitad is at the other house.

notes.title: Shakshuka recipe
notes.text:
Saute a diced onion and two garlic cloves in olive oil, add a teaspoon each of cumin and smoked paprika, then pour in one can of crushed tomatoes. Simmer fifteen minutes until it thickens, and add a chopped green chili if you want heat.
Make little wells with a spoon and crack in four eggs. Cover the pan and cook for about eight minutes so the whites set but the yolks stay runny. Crumble feta on top, sprinkle parsley, and serve straight from the pan with warm bread.

notes.title: Sourdough starter log
notes.text:
I feed the starter every morning with equal weights of starter, flour, and water, a one to one to one ratio. The kitchen sits around 24 degrees, and by the sixth hour it has doubled and smells fruity rather than like nail polish.
To test whether it is ready to bake, I drop a spoonful into a glass of water and see if it floats. The discard goes into weekend pancakes. If the starter turns grey and watery on top, that liquid is hooch, and it just means I fed it too late.

notes.title: Cast iron care
notes.text:
Wash the skillet with hot water and a stiff brush, no soap, then dry it on the stove over low heat until every drop is gone. While it is still warm I wipe on a very thin layer of flaxseed oil and buff off the excess so it does not turn sticky.
To re-season, bake it upside down at 230 degrees for an hour with foil on the rack below to catch drips. If rust appears, scrub with steel wool and vinegar, then season again. Never leave it soaking in the sink overnight.

notes.title: Doro wat prep
notes.text:
Marinate the chicken pieces in lemon juice and salt for an hour. Chop four large red onions finely and cook them down dry in a heavy pot for about an hour, stirring often, before adding any fat.
Add niter kibbeh, three tablespoons of berbere, and garlic, then let it simmer slowly with the chicken. Hard-boiled eggs with a few cuts go in during the last twenty minutes. The recipe makes a big batch, so I freeze half in portions for busy weeks.

notes.title: Meal prep Sunday plan
notes.text:
The goal is five lunch boxes for the work week without spending more than 900 birr. I roast two trays of chickpeas with cumin, cook two cups of rice in the rice cooker, and steam spinach in the last minute so it stays green.
Grocery list for next week: lentils, plain yogurt, spinach, carrots, eggs, and lemons. Lunches keep four days in the fridge, so the Friday box gets frozen on Sunday night and moved to the fridge Thursday.

notes.title: Lalibela trip
notes.text:
The rock-hewn churches are carved downward from the volcanic rock, eleven of them in two main clusters. Bete Giyorgis is the cross-shaped one and looks best in the early morning light. Shoes come off before every entrance, so bring thick socks.
The flight from Addis takes about one hour and a local guide costs around a thousand birr per day. Genna, Ethiopian Christmas on 7 January, is the busiest and most moving time to visit, so book the guesthouse at least two months ahead.

notes.title: Frankfurt relocation checklist
notes.text:
First week: register my address at the Buergeramt within 14 days (Anmeldung) and bring the rental contract plus the landlord confirmation form. Without the registration I cannot open a bank account or get a tax ID.
Still to do: public health insurance enrollment, a Schufa credit report for apartment applications, a monthly regional transit pass, and a German SIM card. Search for flats on ImmoScout early because viewings fill within hours, and keep a folder with passport scans, degree certificates, and the work contract.

notes.title: Danakil depression packing list
notes.text:
Temperatures reach 45 degrees in the daytime, so bring a wide-brim hat, a light scarf, and at least four liters of water per person per day. The Erta Ale hike starts after sunset to avoid the heat and takes about three hours up the lava field.
Bring a headlamp with spare batteries, a thin sleeping sheet, and closed hiking shoes with strong soles. Visitors must travel with an armed escort arranged by the tour operator, and everyone sleeps outside on simple cots near the crater rim.

notes.title: Bahir Dar weekend
notes.text:
Take the early flight instead of the nine-hour bus, it lands in about an hour. Hire a boat on Lake Tana to visit the island monasteries, Ura Kidane Mehret has the best painted walls, and bargain for the full-day price before boarding.
On the second day, ride a bajaj to the bus stop for the Blue Nile Falls, which are strongest right after the rainy season. Eat fresh grilled fish at the lakeside cafe and walk to the Saturday market for coffee beans and woven baskets.

notes.title: Visa paperwork notes
notes.text:
The passport has to be valid for at least six months beyond the trip, with two blank pages. Bring bank statements for the last three months, an employer letter, and a return flight reservation.
Travel insurance must cover at least thirty thousand euros in medical costs. Photos are 35 by 45 millimeters on a light background. Book the embassy appointment early, since processing takes around fifteen working days and the fee is paid in cash at submission.

notes.title: Airport tips
notes.text:
Arrive at Bole three hours before international departures because the security lines and document checks are slow. Keep the power bank in carry-on only, since airlines do not allow it in checked luggage.
For the Istanbul layover of four hours, I keep the boarding pass for the next flight on my phone and a printed copy of the hotel booking in case immigration asks. Buy a local SIM at the arrivals hall, and always pack a change of clothes in the cabin bag in case the suitcase is delayed.

notes.title: Postgres indexing lesson
notes.text:
The orders page was slow, so I ran EXPLAIN ANALYZE and saw a sequential scan across two million rows. Adding a composite index on user_id and created_at brought the query from 800 milliseconds down to 12.
Column order matters: the equality column goes first and the range column second. For the status column that is mostly archived, a partial index with WHERE status = 'active' is smaller and faster. Remember that every index slows down writes, so drop the unused ones.

notes.title: Go concurrency notes
notes.text:
A goroutine leaks when it blocks forever on a channel nobody closes, so every long-running goroutine needs a way to stop through context cancellation. Use sync.WaitGroup to wait for a fixed set of workers and errgroup when the first error should cancel the rest.
For many jobs, start a worker pool of eight goroutines reading from a jobs channel instead of spawning one per item. Run the tests with the race detector enabled to catch unsynchronized map writes before production.

notes.title: JWT auth pitfalls
notes.text:
Keep the access token short-lived, around fifteen minutes, and put the refresh token in an httpOnly cookie so scripts cannot read it. Rotate the refresh token on every use and revoke the whole family if an old one is replayed.
Never place sensitive data in the payload, because it is only base64 encoded and anyone can read it. Always verify the signature and pin the allowed algorithm, otherwise the none algorithm trick lets an attacker forge tokens.

notes.title: Docker compose tips
notes.text:
Add a healthcheck to the database service and use depends_on with condition service_healthy so the backend does not start before Postgres accepts connections. Named volumes keep the data between container restarts, but docker compose down -v deletes them.
Use env_file instead of hard-coding secrets in the compose file. After changing a Dockerfile, run up with the build flag, and prune dangling images from time to time because they eat disk space.

notes.title: Git rebase vs merge
notes.text:
I use interactive rebase to squash fixup commits before opening a pull request so the history reads cleanly. The golden rule: never rebase a branch other people already pulled.
When I must update a branch after rebasing, I push with force-with-lease so I do not overwrite a teammate's work. If I lose commits, git reflog shows where HEAD used to be. And git bisect finds the commit that introduced a regression in a few steps.

notes.title: System design: URL shortener
notes.text:
Generate the short code by base62 encoding an auto-increment id, which avoids collisions without hashing. The system is read heavy, roughly a hundred reads for every write, so cache the hot links in Redis with a time to live.
Use a 301 redirect for permanent links, or 302 when I want to track every click. Add rate limiting per IP to stop abuse, and pre-allocate id ranges to each server so they can issue codes without talking to a central counter.

notes.title: Running plan for the 10k
notes.text:
Three runs a week: an easy run on Tuesday, intervals on Thursday, and the long run on Sunday. I raise the weekly distance by no more than ten percent so the legs can adapt.
Easy pace means I can speak full sentences while moving. Last month a sharp pain along my shin forced a full week of rest and I switched to the pool. The target race is in Addis in November, and I want to finish under fifty-five minutes.

notes.title: Sleep improvement experiment
notes.text:
For two weeks I stopped using screens after ten at night, cooled the bedroom with a fan, and cut caffeine after two in the afternoon. I also woke at six every day, even on weekends.
The watch tracked an average of six hours twenty minutes before and seven hours ten minutes after. Deep sleep rose a little too. The hardest rule was the weekend wake-up time, but the consistent rhythm made mornings much easier.

notes.title: Posture and desk setup
notes.text:
The top of the monitor should sit at eye level, about an arm's length away. A laptop stand with a separate keyboard keeps my neck neutral, and the wrists stay straight when the keyboard is flat.
I follow the 20-20-20 rule, looking at something far away for twenty seconds every twenty minutes, and stand up once an hour. The chair needs lumbar support, and the feet should rest flat on the floor, otherwise my lower back aches by afternoon.

notes.title: Hydration and coffee
notes.text:
Target is two and a half liters of water per day, tracked in a phone app. I drink one cup of coffee after breakfast and switch to tea in the afternoon.
Whenever I skip water in the morning I get a dull headache by noon, so the first glass goes down before anything else. On gym days I add a pinch of salt and a banana to the plan. Sugary sodas are out except on holidays.

notes.title: Strength routine
notes.text:
I follow a push, pull, legs split four days a week. Squats are three sets of five, and every session I try to add 2.5 kilograms to the bar when all reps feel clean, which is progressive overload.
Every sixth week is a deload where I use sixty percent of the weight to let the joints recover. The current goal is ten strict bodyweight pull-ups, and I am at six. Protein target is one hundred and thirty grams a day.

notes.title: Meditation log
notes.text:
Ten minutes every morning before opening the phone. I count breaths from one to ten and start over whenever the mind wanders, which happens constantly; noticing it is the practice itself.
The streak is at twenty-one days. The silent timer works better for me than the guided app, because I stop waiting for the voice. Before the last two interviews I felt calmer and the usual racing thoughts were quieter.

notes.title: Coffee brewing notes
notes.text:
For the morning pour-over I use 20 grams of medium-ground beans with 320 grams of water just off the boil. I bloom for forty seconds, then pour in slow circles until the scale reaches the target.
The brew tastes sour when the grind is too coarse or the water cools too much, while bitterness means I should grind a little larger. I rinse the paper filter first and clean the burr grinder every Sunday so old oils do not spoil the cup.

notes.title: Freezer inventory
notes.text:
Label every container with the dish and date before it goes into the freezer. Soups and stews are portioned into flat bags so they freeze quickly and stack neatly, while cooked rice goes into single-serving boxes.
The oldest meals are in the top drawer: lentil soup from 3 March, two portions of doro wat from 7 March, and tomato sauce from 10 March. Thaw food overnight in the fridge and reheat leftovers until steaming rather than leaving them on the counter.

notes.title: Travel budgeting sheet
notes.text:
For the next trip I split the budget into transport, lodging, food, activities, and a ten percent emergency buffer. I record every purchase in the spreadsheet in the local currency and convert it at the month-end exchange rate.
Cash is useful for small taxis and markets, but I keep a second card in a separate wallet. The daily food allowance is 25 euros, and I check the running total each evening so an expensive tour does not surprise me later.

notes.title: Mountain hike checklist
notes.text:
The day before a long hike I charge the headlamp and phone, download the offline map, and tell someone the route and expected return time. The pack gets two liters of water, a rain shell, first-aid supplies, a whistle, and an extra layer.
I start early to finish exposed ridges before afternoon storms. Trekking poles help on the descent, and I turn around if the weather changes or the remaining daylight is shorter than the route requires.

notes.title: Python testing workflow
notes.text:
Run the focused test file while developing, then run the full suite before opening a pull request. Pytest fixtures provide a temporary database and keep setup out of individual tests.
For flaky tests I capture the seed and rerun the case several times instead of adding a sleep. Coverage is useful for finding untested branches, but a high percentage does not replace assertions about the important behavior. CI runs linting, type checks, and tests on every push.

notes.title: Redis cache design
notes.text:
Cache read-heavy profile responses under a key containing the user id and version, with a fifteen-minute expiration. On an update, delete the key so the next request repopulates it from the database.
Never treat the cache as the source of truth. Use a short lock when many requests miss the same key, and limit value size so one oversized response cannot evict useful entries. Monitor hit rate, memory usage, and evictions after deployment.

notes.title: Weekly meal and exercise log
notes.text:
I schedule strength training on Monday and Thursday, an easy walk on Tuesday, and a longer bike ride on Saturday. Rest days remain on the calendar because recovery is part of the plan rather than a failure.
I write down energy, soreness, and sleep beside each session. If two nights of poor sleep coincide with unusual fatigue, I replace the hard workout with mobility work. The aim is steady consistency, not making up missed sessions with double workouts.

notes.title: Allergy symptom log
notes.text:
During pollen season I record the time of sneezing, itchy eyes, outdoor exposure, and any medicine taken. Keeping the bedroom window closed on high-count mornings and showering after a park visit reduced the evening symptoms.
The air purifier runs on its low setting overnight, and I wash bedding weekly in hot water. If breathing becomes difficult or symptoms change suddenly, I seek medical help instead of changing medication on my own.

notes.title: Bread baking schedule
notes.text:
I mix the dough after dinner and leave it covered on the counter for the first rise. In the morning I shape the loaf, place it in a floured basket, and refrigerate it until the oven and Dutch oven are fully heated.
The covered pot traps steam during the first twenty minutes, then I remove the lid so the crust can brown. I score one deep slash before baking and wait at least an hour after cooling before slicing.

notes.title: Grocery price comparison
notes.text:
I compare the unit price rather than the sticker price when shopping. The neighborhood market has cheaper vegetables, while the supermarket is better for bulk oats and household supplies when there is a discount.
I plan three dinners before leaving, check the pantry first, and bring a reusable bag. A written list prevents impulse snacks, and I record the total afterward to see whether the weekly food budget is holding.

notes.title: Train journey plan
notes.text:
The overnight train leaves at 20:40, so I will arrive at the station thirty minutes early with the ticket saved offline. A small lock secures the backpack, and earplugs and an eye mask should make the sleeper berth more comfortable.
I keep water and a snack within reach, set an alarm before the arrival time, and confirm the platform on the station board. The return ticket is changeable, which is useful if the conference schedule moves.

notes.title: Language study routine
notes.text:
I practice German for twenty-five minutes after breakfast using spaced-repetition cards, then listen to a short news story during the commute. On Wednesdays I meet a conversation partner and write down phrases I could not produce quickly.
The review deck stays small enough to finish daily, and I add new words only after checking an example sentence. Every Sunday I revisit the week's mistakes rather than starting another grammar chapter.

notes.title: API pagination notes
notes.text:
List endpoints use a cursor based on the last record's stable sort key instead of an offset, because inserts can otherwise shift later pages. The response includes the items and a next_cursor that is null when there are no more results.
The server caps page size at one hundred and validates cursors as opaque values. Tests cover an empty page, duplicate prevention across pages, and a record inserted between two requests.

notes.title: Frontend accessibility checklist
notes.text:
Every interactive control needs a visible focus style and a label that a screen reader can understand. Images that convey meaning get useful alt text, while decorative images use an empty alt attribute.
I check keyboard navigation without a mouse, verify color contrast, and make error messages identify the field that needs attention. The page should remain usable when text is zoomed to 200 percent.

notes.title: Morning mobility routine
notes.text:
Before sitting at the desk I spend ten minutes on gentle movement: cat-cow, hip hinges, ankle circles, and a slow thoracic rotation on each side. The goal is to wake up stiff joints, not to force a deep stretch.
I breathe normally and stop if a movement causes sharp pain. On cycling days I add calf raises, while on rest days an easy walk is enough. The routine works best when the mat is already beside the bed.

notes.title: Doctor appointment preparation
notes.text:
Before an appointment I write the main concern, when it began, what makes it better or worse, and every medicine or supplement I take. I bring recent readings and a short list of questions so I do not forget them in the room.
I note the clinician's instructions and the follow-up date before leaving. If a test is ordered, I record where it will happen and whether fasting or other preparation is required.
